title: Isomorphism inverse image preserves the tower domain, normalization and strict roots
statement: Fix the coefficient and normalized tower presentations [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers, def-pur-tower-geometric-purity-data]. For every scheme T and isomorphism g:T to T, inverse image preserves uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor towers, with the same bounds, and preserves normalized towers. For every normalized Tate-tower presentation w and root-line coordinates r, there is a strict Roots comparison along g. The normalization is the scalar restriction/root restriction equation, before localization, at every positive quotient level. No normalization is required for the constructible finite-Tor preservation assertion.

proof.text: Use the sectionwise inverse-image equivalence of a scheme isomorphism on every coefficient ring. The constant-section comparison is fixed, and the inverse equivalence commutes with each quotient transition.

Apply exact inverse image to flat K-flat representatives and their scalar-extension tensors. Etale origin and constructibility are invariant under the site equivalence. Cohomology and Tor intervals stay the same at every coefficient level. Thus the uniform constructible finite-Tor domain is preserved. The canonical reduction arrows are transported to the canonical reduction arrows and hence normalization is preserved.

Use restriction of actual root sections and of scalars on the strict tower, and its inverse along g inverse. These commute with quotient and power transitions. Transport through the supplied w and r identifications. The unit comparison is the fixed constant-section comparison. This gives exactly Roots, including degree zero and empty sites.
